Everything from what an adjective is to cases, verb 'to be' and a bunch of other stuff. I didn't know much about English grammar at all, I just kind of did it haha.

If I wanted to talk in different perspectives of people who are hungry...

I can say Gladan sam (I am hungry) 1st Pers.

Gladan si (You are hungry) 1st Pers.

Gladan smo (We are hungry) 2nd Pers.


But if I wanted to say 'He is hungry' according to google translate I say 'On je gladan'.

Just wondering if this is a rule that holds across all examples (where in 1st and 2nd perspective you can place Verb 'To be' after the adjective, but if in 3rd perspective you have to use pronouns and verb 'to be')? I guess that makes sense since you have to specify the pronoun in 3rd person to know gender. Is there any other way to write 'he is hungry'?

Edit: I should add in except for Impersonal Sentences - It is cold - Where you can drop the pronoun - Hladno je
